v.rationale:
Impl-1 ranks first. Both test suites pass (68 and 32 tests), and Laravel is 13.43.0.

Impl-1 met every requirement, and all of my probes passed: price inputs like '.5' and '+3', the search term kept across page links, slug generation when the slug is taken or the name is only symbols, and newest-by-created_at sorting. One failure was my own fault: the probe left out the hidden is_active input that the real form always sends. On Blade it does what the task focuses on: the shared form is a component, the field wrapper uses $attributes->class, the checkbox is handled correctly, an enum drives both the sort validation and the sort select, and a fixed redirect route on the filter request shows errors on the catalogue page. Its tests are much more thorough, covering every admin route, per-field messages, old input for the select and checkbox, and stable pagination. The only downsides are some ceremony (an observer for slugs, inline styles).

Impl-2 is a little leaner, but probes confirmed three real bugs:
- An unticked 'Active' checkbox comes back checked after a failed submit, so input is not kept as the task requires.
- 'Newest' sorts by id, not created_at.
- A blank slug fails when the slug derived from the name is already taken.

Its invalid-filter redirect can also loop back to the same bad URL, and the filter errors are never shown. It uses an @include partial instead of a form component, hard-codes the sort strings in three places, and has thinner tests that miss these failure paths.

v.rationale: impl-1 ranks first. Both test suites pass (impl-1 68/68, impl-2 32/32), and both have thin controllers, Form Requests, attribute scopes, withQueryString and integer price handling. The ranking comes from two real bugs in impl-2, both confirmed with probe tests. First, a bad filter on the public catalogue causes a redirect loop, because the Form Request redirects back to the URL that just failed. Second, an unchecked 'Active' box comes back checked after a failed submit, because the values set in prepareForValidation never reach old input. impl-1 avoids both: it redirects invalid filters to the plain list and shows the errors there, and it uses a hidden is_active=0 input. impl-1 also has the better Blade structure (form component, @class for invalid fields, built-in pagination view, stock badge component) and much stronger tests, including a pagination tiebreaker check, an N+1 check, unchecked-checkbox persistence and an auth matrix. Its weak points are some ceremony: a slug-generating observer, a currency config file, enum cases read inside a view, and inline styles.

v.rationale: Impl-1 ranks first. Both suites pass (impl-2: 44 tests, impl-1: 34). Both cover every lockout path: password login, token issue, reset links, live session, remember cookie and API token. Probes confirmed this once guards were reset between requests. The deciding bug is in impl-2: it never pins the reset-link host, so a forged Host header puts the attacker's domain in the emailed link, which leaks the reset token. Impl-1 calls trustHosts() and builds the link from app.url. Impl-2 is also heavier: one middleware switches on a string to cover two cases and repeats Sanctum's token check, and on the public token endpoint that check returns 401 when a stale bearer header is sent. Impl-1's 'blocked_at' => null credentials are simpler and more idiomatic. Its weak points are minor: a hard-coded sessions table and a group-scoped API middleware.

v.rationale: I ranked impl-1 first by a small margin. Both implementations are nearly identical in structure: Laravel 13 attributes, an observer for the slug and published_at, route ->can() so non-authors get 403 before validation, createOrFirst plus sync for tags, and form requests for index, store and update. All 26 tests pass in each. Probes found no real bugs in either. Null status and null tags both return 422, blank tags return 422, and a symbols-only title falls back to the 'post' slug. Both treat tag names as case-sensitive. impl-1 wins on idioms: index uses $request->enum() with when() and a typed enum scope, its route and test code is cleaner, and it eager-loads only tags:id,name. impl-2 has stricter tag validation, deterministic tag order and slightly stronger ordering and pagination tests. Against that, its scopes take nullable strings and contain the conditional, its route definitions mix two styles, and its tests carry extra ceremony (Http::preventStrayRequests, the \DB alias).

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-2 first by a small margin. Both implementations pass their own 26 tests, and the code is almost the same: same migration, enum, observer, policy, route-level ->can(), createOrFirst plus sync, and #[Scope] attributes.

The two edge-case probes per implementation, plus extra checks, all behaved correctly in both:
- Cycling a post published → draft → published keeps the original published_at.
- tags: null and status: null both return 422.
- An empty tag filter returns 200 with the full list.

The deciding difference is duplicate tags. impl-1 accepted ['php',' php ','PHP'] and created two tags, 'php' and 'PHP'. impl-2 rejects duplicates at validation with distinct:ignore_case and returns tag names in sorted order.

impl-1 also has a guest-redirect fallback to a 'login' route that doesn't exist; it is unused now but would break any future non-API auth route. Its routes are unnamed.

impl-1 does have a cleaner newestFirst scope, typed scope arguments, and model-side trim and dedupe. impl-2's scopes take nullable arguments, its tests include small bits of ceremony, and it rejects duplicate tags rather than merging them, which is strict.

Overall, impl-2 handles tag input better at the boundary and its API output is more predictable.

v.rationale: The two implementations are very close: same Filament 5 resource layout, enums with HasLabel/HasColor, observer-driven resolved_at, attribute-based scopes, and full test suites that pass (impl-1: 40 tests, impl-2: 31). The ranking comes down to one real bug. In impl-1, tickets cascade-delete with their customer, and any non-admin can delete customers.
